newsitem.title: UK: Dixons boosts current sales, adds jobs.
newsitem.headline: Dixons boosts current sales, adds jobs.

text.p: Britain's leading electricals retailer Dixons Group Plc said on Wednesday it will create 3,000 new jobs in 1997/98 and said windfall gains from building society flotations had boosted sales in the past nine weeks.

The retailer said retail division sales had increased by 32 percent overall during the period, and by 17 percent on a like-for-like basis. The group said it expected to create around 3,000 new jobs over the year, about the same number as in the previous 12 months.
Chairman Sir Stanley Kalms said the sales improvement, which followed strong growth in the comparable period last year, was broadly spread across product categories.

"The windfall gains from demutualisation have had an impact on these figures," Kalms said in a statement. He cautioned that the current sales trend should not be extrapolated for the financial year as a whole.
But he said the group anticipated another good year, against a background of rising interest rates. He said the group's gross margins had remained stable.
The company reported profits before tax and exceptional items for the 53 weeks to May 3 1997 of 190.2 million pounds ($321 million), up from 135.2 million in the previous year.
Dixons said personal computers and related products increased their share of the group's sales to 29 percent from 23 percent, mainly due to the rapid expansion of its PC World out-of-town stores.
Total sales from the retail division rose to 2.4 billion pounds, from 1.9 billion. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
